name: Delaware
overview: Delaware's statewide senior-credit framework allows school districts to authorize a credit against regular school property taxes on a qualifying principal residence.

programs.name: Senior School Property Tax Credit
programs.ageRule: Age 65+ as of June 30 immediately before the county fiscal year.
programs.incomeDefinition: Not income-tested under the statewide program.
programs.incomeLimits: No income limit listed for the statewide credit.
programs.maximumBenefit: Statutory ceiling is 50% of eligible regular school property tax, up to $500; district authorization can provide less.
programs.formulaSummary: District-authorized nonrefundable bill credit, no greater than the lesser of half the eligible regular school levy after applicable reductions or $500.
programs.application: Apply to county ordinarily by April 30; annual reapplication generally unnecessary. A statutory financial-disability filing-date waiver may apply.
eligibilityNotes: Residency waiting periods depend on when Delaware domicile began; newer arrivals generally require ten consecutive years. Statute measures the required duration on June 30 immediately before the county fiscal year.
Prior-year property taxes must have been paid in full.
Actual school-district authorization and eligible school-tax amounts must be established; the statewide ceiling is not an automatic award.
interactions: County exemptions and disabled-veteran relief require separate review.
programs.programYear: 2025 application cohort: ordinary filing by April 30, 2025 and age/domicile qualification on June 30, 2025 for the upcoming county fiscal year. County bill periods require separate identification.

researchNotes: A legislative fiscal note proposing a higher cap is not evidence of enactment; the agency overview states $500.
Statewide framework describes the governing law, not verified adoption in every district. No complete 2025 district-authorization registry was established by this source review.

The linked form measures domicile duration before application, while statute uses June 30 before the county fiscal year. This inventory follows the statutory date; district, property and billing facts remain necessary for any calculation.
